steps.body: To compare two decimals, line up their points and check place by place, **left to right**. The first place where the digits differ decides it — a bigger digit there wins, no matter what follows. Start at tenths, the biggest place after the point.

options.feedback: The tenths digits are 6 and 4; 6 is bigger, so 0.6 wins.
Compare the tenths first: 4 vs 6. Since 4 is smaller, 0.4 is the lesser one — 0.6 is greater.

options.label: They're equal
options.feedback: Their tenths digits differ (6 vs 4), so they can't be equal. 0.6 is greater.

hints: Look at the tenths place first.
explanationVariants: Tenths decide it: 6 > 4, so 0.6 is greater.
The first place already differs, and 6 beats 4.
Tenths tie at 3, so move to hundredths: 5 vs 8 — 0.38 is greater.
Equal tenths pushes the decision to the next place, hundredths.

widget.successFeedback: Tenths tie (both 3), so hundredths decide: 8 > 5, making 0.38 greater.
widget.gtFeedback: The tenths tie at 3, so check hundredths: 5 vs 8. Since 5 is smaller, 0.35 is the lesser — 0.38 wins.
widget.eqFeedback: The hundredths differ (5 vs 8), so they aren't equal. 0.38 is greater.

steps.body: Here's the trap: more digits does **not** mean bigger. Compare 0.7 and 0.68 at the first place — tenths: 7 versus 6. 7 wins immediately, so **0.7 is greater than 0.68**, even though 0.68 has more digits. The first differing place is all that matters.

explanationVariants: Tenths decide: 7 > 6, so 0.7 beats 0.68 despite having fewer digits.
The extra digit in 0.68 never matters — the tenths already settled it.

widget.successFeedback: Tenths first: 7 vs 6. 7 wins, so 0.7 is greater — the extra digit in 0.68 doesn't help.
widget.ltFeedback: Length is the trap here. Compare tenths: 7 vs 6 — 0.7 already wins before the 8 matters.
widget.eqFeedback: The tenths already differ (7 vs 6), so they can't be equal — 0.7 is greater.

options.feedback: Tenths tie at 5. In hundredths, 0.52 has a 2 and 0.5 has nothing (a 0), so 0.52 is greater.
Tenths tie at 5, so check hundredths: 0.52 has 2 there, 0.5 has 0. 0.52 is greater.

options.label: They're equal
options.feedback: 0.52 carries an extra 2 in hundredths that 0.5 lacks, so they differ. 0.52 is greater.

hints: Think of 0.5 as 0.50 to compare hundredths.
explanationVariants: Tenths tie, then hundredths: 2 > 0, so 0.52 wins.
Reading 0.5 as 0.50 shows the hundredths gap.
The very first place already separates them: 0.6 is greater.

widget.prompt: In comparing 0.61 and 0.48, which place decides the winner?

options.label: The tenths place (6 vs 4)
options.feedback: 6 and 4 differ right at the tenths, so that decides it — 0.61 is greater, and the hundredths never matter.

options.label: The hundredths place (1 vs 8)
options.feedback: You only reach hundredths if tenths tie. Here tenths already differ (6 vs 4), so tenths decide.

options.label: Neither — count the digits
options.feedback: Digit count doesn't decide comparisons. The first differing place — tenths, 6 vs 4 — does.

hints: Pad the shorter one: think of 0.41 as 0.410.
0.409 has 0 in hundredths, 0.410 has 1 — so 0.41 is bigger.
explanationVariants: Tenths tie at 4. In hundredths, 0.409 has 0 and 0.41 (=0.410) has 1, so 0.41 is greater.
Reading 0.41 as 0.410, the hundredths 1 > 0 settles it: 0.41 is greater.

widget.successFeedback: Read 0.41 as 0.410. Tenths tie at 4; hundredths give 1 vs 0, so 0.41 is greater.
widget.gtFeedback: The length is the trap. Pad to 0.409 vs 0.410: tenths tie, then hundredths 0 vs 1 — 0.41 wins.
widget.eqFeedback: Pad 0.41 to 0.410: tenths tie at 4, but the hundredths differ (1 vs 0) — not equal.

steps.body: Left to right, first difference wins.
takeaways: Line up the decimal points and compare place by place, starting at tenths.
The first place where digits differ decides — later places don't matter.
More digits does not mean bigger: 0.7 is greater than 0.68.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Compare decimals place by place from the left; the first differing place decides.** For 0.8 vs 0.3, the tenths (8 vs 3) differ right away, so 0.8 is greater. Always start at the biggest place — tenths.

explanationVariants: The first place already differs — 0.8 wins.

options.feedback: Compare the tenths: 3 vs 8. Since 3 is smaller, 0.8 is greater.

options.label: Equal
options.feedback: The tenths differ (8 vs 3), so they aren't equal. 0.8 is greater.
